citation.title: On the relationship between mind perception and social support of chatbots

reading.source_scope_note: A short randomized support-content experiment with137 Korean adults using a scripted Facebook Messenger chatbot. Mind-attribution measures occur after interaction and perceived message effectiveness. Added informational or emotional support is compared with an active questioning/disclosure baseline. Outcome is subjective helpfulness/effectiveness,not therapy efficacy,actual stress resolution or objective information quality.
access_limits: All supplied text,table and figures read. No public supplement identified. Data are explicitly not readily available because conversations are confidential and some participants did not consent to research sharing. No data requested,private access attempted or author contact made.

Full conversation scripts,message lengths,condition-specific error rates,cell sample sizes and coding records unavailable. Raw-data/group-classification reconstruction and full ANOVA reproduction not claimed.

Kwon2017 Psychology of Human Relationships,House/Cohen/Hobfoll social-support sources,Banks task/codebook and cited clinical chatbot studies were not independently fully read. The article’s citation/adaptation does not supply independent book or original-study credit.

The referenced CHI social-support metadata appears to duplicate name components. Institutional PDF retrieval returned403;exact byline repair deferred rather than copied from malformed Crossref fields.
The study’s deliberate cartoon explanation is called implicit mind perception by its authors;no independent awareness or automaticity validation was obtained.

study.sample: 163 recruited through online systems/communities,26 incomplete excluded,final137;56.2%female,meanage23.3,SD6.1,range18–49,all Korean,43.1%prior chatbot use. Random groups:42base,48informational,47emotional. Compensation credit/voucher/payment. SNU ethics2109/002–031 and online consent stated.
study.system: Chatfuel script-based chatbot in Facebook Messenger with Dialogflow relationship/emotion classification. Humanlike name Allen,image,first-person language,varied acknowledgments,typing indicators and1–6second delays used across conditions. These cues were not independently randomized. This is not a modern open-ended LLM therapy system or a tested privacy guarantee.
study.conditions: All groups receive questions about an interpersonal stress event,thoughts,feelings,behavior and possible changes. Added informational advice varies by relationship building/maintaining/ending;emotional condition adds understanding and encouragement. Base is active reflective disclosure,not absence of support. Advice and empathetic language are general;authors disclose classification errors.
study.outcome: Four translated7-point message-effectiveness items,alpha.86,mean4.4,SD1.3,including effective/helpful judgments. No independent accuracy,clinical symptoms,sustained stress change,behavioral coping or adverse-outcome endpoint.
study.mind_measures: Explicit four-item composite:two agency/two pain-fear experience items,alpha.87. Dichotomy uses mean>3,n82 versus55. White-lie cartoon asks whether the chatbot lied and why;raters code mental-state explanation1 versus algorithm-only0,kappa.86,n83versus54. This operational proxy is not direct evidence of unconscious thought,accurate mentalizing or actual chatbot feeling.
study.timing: Support content randomized;mind perception measured after message effectiveness,explicit before cartoon. Mind groups are post-treatment classifications,not randomized baseline moderators. Reverse interpretation,priming and response consistency remain possible;authors acknowledge no causal mind-perception test.
study.tests: Pooled mind-group t tests show higher helpfulness for explicit and coded-mental-state groups. Separate2×2ANOVAs compare base/informational and base/emotional,each with measured mind group. Informational interactionF1.26,p.264;emotional interactionF6.31,p.014,partialeta.07. Explicit interactions null. Emotional versus base main contrasts favor base;informational versus base contrasts null.
study.comparison_limit: A formal emotional-versus-base interaction exists. However,one significant interaction and one null interaction in separate overlapping subsets do not directly establish an emotional-versus-informational interaction. No full three-level support×mind test or direct contrast is reported. Nulls do not prove equal effectiveness or establish mind as necessary.
study.content_check: Within informational support,relationship-phase means round to4.6 andANOVAF≈0,p.999. This does not rule out every content,classification,length or context confound and is not an equivalence test.
study.priming_limit: Nearly40%classified nonmentalizing after explicit questions does not rule out priming in others. No randomized order comparison. An explained mental-state attribution can be deliberate despite its implicit label.
study.power: Retrospective detectability claims include65%power for medium ANOVA effects and are acknowledged as limited. They do not establish an a priori powered clinical endpoint or general safety.

welch_check.boundary: No raw-data repair or cause inferred; different actual counts,SDs,group labels or statistic transcription require output.

summary: Add Social support with informational and emotional subtypes linked to their parent. Separate helping resources from communication orientation and felt empathy. Retain the active baseline,post-treatment mind measures,perceived-only outcome and actual emotional-versus-base interaction. Stronger direct support-type,automaticity,clinical-benefit and necessity claims are not established. Clarify threshold logic and a verified venue identity without inventing raw classifications or private evidence.

findings.definition: Providing resources through social interaction to help someone cope with stress or other demands.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Scripted chatbot support offered experimentally; human helpfulness ratings, not clinical efficacy or machine feelings
findings.novelty_rationale: A defined resource or helping function, distinct from conversational style, actual empathy, mutual emotional reciprocity and a recipient’s trust. Parent and subtype links make intentional conceptual overlap explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The article defines support broadly and compares reflective questioning with added information/advice or understanding/encouragement. Participants rate short conversations;the experiment does not test every support resource or demonstrate lasting benefit.
findings.boundary: Offered support,perceived helpfulness,actual benefit,professional treatment and mutual care differ. More support is not automatically better;respect consent,context and the person’s requested help.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether offered resources match the person’s stated needs while measuring factual quality,perceived helpfulness and appropriate follow-up separately. Keep limits and human options clear;do not claim clinical outcomes from favorable ratings.

findings.definition: Providing advice or information intended to help someone understand, manage or resolve a problem.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Scripted chatbot support offered experimentally; human helpfulness ratings, not clinical efficacy or machine feelings
findings.novelty_rationale: A defined resource or helping function, distinct from conversational style, actual empathy, mutual emotional reciprocity and a recipient’s trust. Parent and subtype links make intentional conceptual overlap explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The randomized informational condition adds general relationship advice to reflective questions. It is not significantly more helpful than base in the reported pairwise analyses;the study does not establish objective advice accuracy or superiority over emotional support.
findings.boundary: Relevant advice can be helpful or mistaken. Informational support is a resource function,not necessarily terse task-oriented style. Verify claims,match scope and avoid substituting unqualified advice for appropriate professional help.
findings.ai_proposal: Assess whether advice is relevant,evidence-grounded and usable in the given situation. Compare equivalent factual resources with acknowledgment or question-only alternatives without presuming one format is universally preferable.

findings.definition: Expressing understanding, care or encouragement to help another person feel valued and supported.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Scripted chatbot support offered experimentally; human helpfulness ratings, not clinical efficacy or machine feelings
findings.novelty_rationale: A defined resource or helping function, distinct from conversational style, actual empathy, mutual emotional reciprocity and a recipient’s trust. Parent and subtype links make intentional conceptual overlap explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The emotional condition adds scripted understanding/encouragement. Its association with a coded mental-state explanation differs from base,with a significant interaction. Added emotional scripts are rated less effective than active base overall in the reported contrasts;mind attribution is measured afterward.
findings.boundary: Supportive expression is not proof of felt empathy,actual understanding or a reciprocal bond. Do not pretend to have human feelings,pressure attachment or infer that all emotional support requires anthropomorphism. Tailor to the person’s preferences without overstating benefit.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare appropriate acknowledgment and encouragement with reflective listening and informational help. Hold factual content and interaction burden as steady as possible;assess understanding,comfort and unwanted pressure separately from subjective warmth.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution or communication construct; add the scripted support experiment and its measurement boundaries rather than a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: Explicit agency/experience ratings and coded explanations of a white-lie cartoon are post-interaction mind-attribution proxies. They associate with helpfulness ratings,with a support-dependent pattern for the coded proxy versus base.
findings.boundary: Combined explicit scores and one coded task do not validate all dimensions,unconscious mind attribution,causal moderation or chatbot feeling. The grouping is post-treatment and threshold-dependent.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution or communication construct; add the scripted support experiment and its measurement boundaries rather than a synonym.

evidence.quote: actively thinking about how to respond

findings.evidence_scope: Raters classify whether a participant explains a fictional chatbot white lie using an internal mental state rather than only an algorithm. Agreementkappa.86 supports coding consistency,not accuracy or automaticity of the inferred process.
findings.boundary: Explicitly explaining a cartoon can be deliberate;mentalistic language does not prove the agent actually has the attributed state. One task adapted from robot research does not validate a universal implicit-ToM measure.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution or communication construct; add the scripted support experiment and its measurement boundaries rather than a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The system uses a humanlike name/image,first-person phrasing,typing cues,varied messages and contextual classification to encourage social responses. These are common setup features,not separately randomized causes in this study.
findings.boundary: Humanlike presentation,perceived mind,empathic wording and actual capacity differ. Results do not authorize false human identity,unverified confidentiality promises or engineering attachment as a therapeutic requirement.

findings.definition: A mutual exchange of care, warmth and empathic responses in an interaction.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution or communication construct; add the scripted support experiment and its measurement boundaries rather than a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion theorizes that emotional support may prompt expectations of shared feeling. The experiment delivers scripted messages and collects recipient ratings;it does not observe mutual felt care or a relationship obligation.
findings.boundary: Boundary note only. One-way emotional support differs from reciprocity;an appreciative response does not require emotional repayment or demonstrate AI feelings. No independent measured-reciprocity credit.

source_corrections.correction: One item≥4 does not imply a four-item mean>3;for example4,1,1,1has mean1.75. State the actual aggregate rule separately from any item-level rule. Raw data/code are unavailable,so no participant is reassigned and reported group counts remain as published.
source_corrections.scope: Logical clarification of the stated threshold,not a reanalysis.

source_corrections.correction: The DOI identifies Technology,Mind,and Behavior1(2),101–113,with publisher citation/Crossref year2020. Repair the journal homonym;distinguish this issue citation from possible2021online/upload records rather than invent a different article. Original full text was not independently read.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Prediction explicitly compares informational and emotional support,but reported interactions separately compare each with base. A direct support-type interaction contrast is not supplied. Retain the real emotional/base result without calling the missing contrast significant.

Coding an openly requested explanation does not demonstrate lack of awareness or automaticity. The proportion not coded mentalistic cannot by itself establish no priming from preceding explicit questions. Authors acknowledge the one-task limitation;no replacement classification is invented.

Reported mind-group mainF≈.01 in models with an interaction requires factor coding,sum-of-squares choice and exact cell counts for full reconstruction. Published cell means alone do not establish an erroneousF or group equivalence;output unavailable.

Bae Brandtzæg/P.B.andKristoffer Dysthe/K.K.fields duplicate given-name components in Crossref too. A primary indexed repository byline differs,but its PDF retrieval returned403. Exact full-name normalization deferred until the primary byline is inspected;the validpaperDOI10.1145/3411764.3445318 is retained.

Allowing one-decimalSD rounding gives approximately82.64–94.49,still short of the printeddf. Different actual counts,SDs,group labels or transcription could explain;raw output unavailable,so no repaired count/statistic or misconduct inference.

source_identity_checks.finding: DOI10.1145/3411764.3445318 verifies the title and real2021CHI publication,1–13. Malformed author slots do not imply a nonexistent paper. Original not fully read.

The article explicitly restricts conversation data because of confidentiality and partial lack of sharing consent. It also acknowledges reuse of parts of Lee2022master’s thesis. No private data sought and thesis/journal are not counted as independent replications.

methodological_limits: Randomized support content is distinct from measured,post-treatment mind groups. Direction,causal mind effects and stable baseline moderation are not identified.
Short young Korean sample,26 incomplete exclusions,one scripted chatbot and generalized content limit transfer to other users,current LLMs and sustained support.
Active questioning/disclosure baseline already provides support. Null informational/base contrast does not prove equal efficacy or a universal informational advantage.
A real emotional/base interaction does not test the stronger emotional/informational contrast. Selected standardFtails/partial-eta values agree;no general numerical failure is inferred.

One overt white-lie explanation and a thresholded four-item composite need validity and coding scope. Reliability is not proof of accurate or unconscious mentalizing;fixed measurement order may prime responses.
Perceived helpfulness does not measure advice truth,clinical improvement,actual emotional understanding or safety. Claimed confidentiality in the experimental script was not independently audited.
Private conversation data and incomplete sharing consent are respected. Cited books,thesis and clinical trials are not claimed as independently read or replicated.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Task/social communication describes interaction orientation;informational/emotional support describes resources offered. They can combine and should not be collapsed into exact synonyms.
Associations or favorable ratings do not establish necessity,sufficiency,actual adoption or clinical benefit. Combined body/agency/experience item choices constrain what mind means.

Check the exact interaction contrasted. Here emotional/base moderation exists,but a direct emotional/informational moderation test is absent;this differs from the formal source/exclusion test in Lee2026.

deferred.term: Implicit mind perception as a separate validated mechanism
deferred.reason: This single overt explanation proxy is not unique evidence for unconscious mentalizing. Keep measure-specific refinement with existing mind perception/ToM.

deferred.term: Expressive writing / introspection as a proven mechanism here
deferred.reason: Base questioning invites writing,but no no-writing comparison or causal mediator separates the proposed mechanism. Preserve the active-control explanation without adding an inferred effect.

limitations: Three linked support constructs,not three claims of clinical efficacy. No unread-book credit,private-data access,automatic harm/principle links,forced paper quota or invented annual totals.
